title: "Visualization"

This document serves as the **main exploratory visualization file** for dataset (daily records from 2013 to 2025). The primary goal is to **discover patterns, trends, anomalies, and potential relationships** in the data through various visualization techniques and statistical summaries.

Different plotting methods, smoothing techniques, comparative overlays (especially highlighting Ramadan periods), rolling statistics, trend analysis, extreme event detection, and hypothesis-driven comparisons are used to uncover possible seasonal behaviors, long-term changes, and month-specific phenomena.

All visualizations and summaries are **exploratory** — they aim to reveal insights rather than test formal hypotheses (although some informal hypotheses are discussed).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library("tidyverse")
library("lubridate")
library("broom")
library("trend")
library("Kendall") 
```

## Loading the cleaned dataset
The cleaned dataset is loaded from CSV. This file contains daily weather variables including temperature, humidity, wind speed, heat index, VPD, etc.
```{r echo=TRUE, message=FALSE}
my_data <- readr::read_csv('D:/climetr/climetr_analysis/datasets/birjand_clean_dataset.csv')
```

## Long-term temperature overview (2013–2025)
This line + smooth plot shows the overall temperature behavior across the entire period, helping to visually identify any long-term warming or seasonal patterns.
```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
my_data %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c), 
            linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey60") +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c),
              method = "loess",
              span = 0.4,
              se = FALSE,
              color = "red", 
              linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year", 
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Mean Daily Temperature – Birjand (2013–2025)",
       x = "Year", y = "Temperature (C°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Yearly temperature with Ramadan highlight (selected year)
We repeat the same visualization approach for humidity, wind speed, dew point, daily temperature range, VPD, Heat Index, and Thermal Discomfort Delta — all for a representative year (2024) with a loess smoothing overlay. The Ramadan period is highlighted in red purely for visual reference, allowing easy inspection of seasonal patterns and overall annual behavior across multiple variables.
```{r}
selected_year <- 2024

my_data %>% filter(year == selected_year) %>% ggplot() +
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x=full_date, y=temp_air_mean_c)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(my_data, year == selected_year & is_ramadan == TRUE), mapping = aes(x=full_date, y=temp_air_mean_c), color="red") +
    geom_smooth(aes(x = full_date, y = temp_air_mean_c),
              method = "loess",
              span = 0.4,
              se = FALSE,
              color = "gray50", 
              linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(title = paste("Daily Mean Temperature –", selected_year),
       subtitle = "Red segment = Ramadan period", x = "Month", y = "Temperature (C°)")
```

## Recent temperatures comparations from 2021-2025
This plot overlays loess-smoothed daily mean temperature curves for the last five years (2021–2025), allowing direct visual comparison of seasonal patterns and inter-annual differences.
```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
my_colors <- c(
  "2021" = "#1f77b4",
  "2022" = "#ff7f0e",
  "2023" = "#2ca02c",
  "2024" = "#d62728",
  "2025" = "#9467bd"
)

start_year <- 2021
end_year   <- 2025

p <- ggplot() +
  
  lapply(start_year:end_year, function(yr) {
    geom_smooth(
      data = filter(my_data, year == yr),
      aes(x    = day_of_year,
          y    = temp_air_mean_c,
          color = factor(yr, levels = start_year:end_year)),   # ← مهم
      method   = "loess",
      span     = 0.4,
      se       = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.6,
      show.legend = TRUE
    )
  }) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = my_colors,
    name   = "Year",
    labels = as.character(start_year:end_year)
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 366, by = 30),
    limits = c(1, 366),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Loess Smoothed Daily Mean Temperature (", start_year, "–", end_year, ")"),
    x        = "Day of Year",
    y        = "Temperature (C°)",
    color    = "Year"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position       = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification  = c("right", "top"),
    legend.background     = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "gray80", linewidth = 0.4),
    legend.title          = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text           = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor.x    = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position   = "plot"
  )

print(p)
```

## Comparing end-of-Ramadan rolling average to previous years
For each year, we take the rolling 30-day average temperature on the last day of Ramadan and compare it to the same day-of-year in all previous years. This helps answer: "Was the temperature at the end of Ramadan in year X unusually warm or cold compared to historical values on the same calendar date?". our last day of Ramadan is pointed with red "x".
```{r}
top_padding <- 0.2
start_date <- 2013
end_date <- 2025
plots <- c()

for (ith_year in end_date:(start_date + 1)) {
  ramadan_data <- my_data %>% 
    filter(year == ith_year & is_ramadan == TRUE) %>% 
    select(day_of_year, full_date, rolling_avg_30)
  
  last_day_index <- which.max(ramadan_data$day_of_year)
  last_day_doy <- ramadan_data$day_of_year[last_day_index]
  last_day_date <- ramadan_data$full_date[last_day_index]
  ramadan_temperature <- ramadan_data$rolling_avg_30[last_day_index]
  
  data <- my_data %>% 
    filter(day_of_year == last_day_doy & year >= start_date & year <= ith_year) %>% 
    select(day_of_year, full_date, year, rolling_avg_30)
  
  the_plot <- data %>% 
    ggplot() +
    geom_point(aes(x = full_date, y = rolling_avg_30), color = "blue") +
    labs(title = paste0("30-day Rolling Avg on Last Day of Ramadan ", ith_year, " vs Past Years"),
         subtitle = paste0("Comparing end-of-Ramadan temperature of ", ith_year, " to same date in previous years"), x = "Year", y = "30-day Rolling Avgerage Temperature (C°)",) +
    annotate("text", x = last_day_date, y = ramadan_temperature, 
             label = "x", color = "red") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "12 month", date_labels = "%Y") +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-40, 40, 5)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean(data$rolling_avg_30), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = mean(data$full_date), y = mean(data$rolling_avg_30) + top_padding,
             label = paste0("Historical Mean = ", round(mean(data$rolling_avg_30), 2)), color = "darkgreen") +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 20, 20))
  
  # Add value labels for each point
  for (idx in 1:nrow(data)) {
    the_plot <- the_plot + 
      annotate("text", x = data[[idx, "full_date"]], 
               y = data[[idx, "rolling_avg_30"]] + top_padding,
               label = round(data[[idx, "rolling_avg_30"]], 2), angle = 0)
  }
  
  plots <- c(plots, the_plot)
}

plots
```



## Monthly mean Heat Index trends across years
This section calculates the mean Heat Index for each month across all years and fits linear trends to detect whether specific months are experiencing systematic warming or cooling over time.
```{r}
data <- tibble()
plots <- c()
all_years <- levels(as.factor(my_data$year))

for (month in 1:12) {
  temp_data <- tibble()
  for (year in all_years) {
    start_date <- ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-", "01"))
    end_date <- ceiling_date(start_date, "month") - days(1)
    
    period <- my_data %>% filter(full_date >= start_date & full_date <= end_date)
    
    mean_temperature <- mean(period$temp_air_mean_c, na.rm = TRUE) 
    mean_heat_index <- mean(period$HI_standard, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    temp_data <- rbind(temp_data, tibble(year=year(start_date), month=month(start_date), mean_temperature=mean_temperature, mean_heat_index=mean_heat_index))
  }

  the_plot = temp_data %>% ggplot() +
geom_line(aes(x = year, y = mean_heat_index), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6) +
geom_smooth(
  aes(x = year, y = mean_heat_index),
  method = "lm",
  se = FALSE, 
  color = "red", linewidth = 1.3, linetype = "solid"
) +
geom_point(aes(x = year, y = mean_heat_index), color = "darkblue", size = 2.2) +
labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean Heat Index (C°)", 
         title = paste0("Mean Heat Index Trend – ", month.name[month]),
         subtitle = paste0(month.name[month], " from ", min(all_years), " to ", max(all_years))) +
    scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(temp_data$year), max(temp_data$year), by = 1),
    labels = function(x) floor(x)
  ) +
geom_text(
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_heat_index,
    label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_heat_index),
    color = mean_heat_index > mean(mean_heat_index, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  vjust = -0.6,
  size = 3.5
) +
scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "red"), guide = "none")
  plots <- c(plots, the_plot)
  
  data <- rbind(data, temp_data)
}
plots
```

## Statistical trend summary per month
We fit linear models and perform Mann-Kendall tests on monthly mean Heat Index to formally identify which months show significant long-term warming or cooling.
```{r}
analyze_trend <- function(df_month) {
  
  # Early exit if too few years → regression not meaningful
  if (nrow(df_month) < 3) {
    return(tibble(
      month = unique(df_month$month),
      note  = "Fewer than 3 years of data"
    ))
  }
  
  # Linear model: temperature ~ year
  model <- lm(mean_heat_index ~ year, data = df_month)
  
  slope     <- coef(model)[2]
  p_value   <- glance(model)$p.value
  r_squared <- glance(model)$r.squared
  years     <- max(df_month$year) - min(df_month$year) + 1
  total_change <- slope * (years - 1)
  
  # Non-parametric trend test
  mk_test <- MannKendall(df_month$mean_heat_index)
  
  # Decide trend category using both parametric (lm) and non-parametric (MK) results
  trend_type <- case_when(
    p_value > 0.05 & mk_test$sl > 0.05   ~ "No significant trend",
    slope > 0   & mk_test$sl <= 0.05     ~ "Significant increasing trend",
    slope < 0   & mk_test$sl <= 0.05     ~ "Significant decreasing trend",
    TRUE                                 ~ "Weak or oscillating trend"
  )
  
  # Return summary row
  tibble(
    month          = unique(df_month$month),
    slope_per_year = round(slope, 4),
    total_change   = round(total_change, 2),
    lm_p           = round(p_value, 4),
    mk_p           = round(mk_test$sl, 4),
    mk_tau         = round(mk_test$tau, 3),
    trend          = trend_type
  )
}

trend_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map_dfr(analyze_trend) %>%
  arrange(month)

print(trend_summary)
```


## Extreme temperature days by month (hot vs cold)
We identify days with extreme heat or cold (defined earlier using 30-day rolling mean ± 2 SD) and count how many such days occurred in each month across all years.
```{r}
extreme_temperature_days <- my_data %>% 
  filter(is_extreme_hot == TRUE | is_extreme_cold == TRUE)

result_wide <- extreme_temperature_days %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = month(full_date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(month_name) %>%
  summarise(
    very_hot  = sum(is_extreme_hot,  na.rm = TRUE),
    very_cold = sum(is_extreme_cold, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month.name)
  )

  result_long <- result_wide %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(very_hot, very_cold),
      names_to = "temperature_type",
      values_to = "count"
    )

ggplot(result_long, aes(x = month_name, y = count, fill = temperature_type)) +
  
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), width = 0.35) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = count,
      y = count
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.70),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("very_hot"   = "#d73027", 
               "very_cold" = "#4575b4"),
    labels = c("very_hot"   = "Very Hot", 
               "very_cold" = "Very Cold")
  ) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Month") +
  
  labs(
    y = "Number of Days",
    title = "Number of Extreme Hot and Cold Days by Month",
    subtitle = "Only days with extreme temperatures (no year separation)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```



## ??
To identify cities with the highest temperature extremes during Ramadan, we calculated two key metrics:

- **Percentage of extreme temperature days within Ramadan**  
  (Number of extreme days during Ramadan ÷ Total number of Ramadan days across the period)  
  This ratio shows how frequently extreme conditions (very hot or very cold) occurred during Ramadan. It is a fair metric for comparing cities, as the number of Ramadan days is roughly consistent each year.

- **Year-by-year comparison of extreme days**  
  A bar chart compares the total number of extreme days in each full year against the number of extreme days occurring only during Ramadan in the same year. This helps visualize whether Ramadan periods contributed disproportionately to annual extremes in specific years.

#### Calculate percentage of extreme days during Ramadan (full period)
This code computes the overall proportion of Ramadan days that were classified as extreme.

```{r}
extreme_temperature_ramadan_days <- my_data %>%
  filter(is_ramadan == TRUE & (is_extreme_hot == TRUE | is_extreme_cold == TRUE))

ramadan_days_total <- my_data %>% filter(is_ramadan == TRUE)

ramadan_extreme_ratio <- nrow(extreme_temperature_ramadan_days) / nrow(ramadan_days_total)

print(paste("Percentage of extreme days during Ramadan:", round(ramadan_extreme_ratio * 100, 1), "%"))
```

## Year-by-year comparison: Extreme days in Ramadan vs. full year
This bar chart shows, for each year, the total number of extreme temperature days in the entire year versus the subset that occurred during Ramadan. It highlights years in which Ramadan had an unusually high share of extremes.
```{r}
yearly_summary <- my_data %>%
  mutate(year = year(full_date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_extreme = sum(is_extreme_hot | is_extreme_cold, na.rm = TRUE),
    ramadan_extreme = sum((is_extreme_hot | is_extreme_cold) & is_ramadan, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(total_extreme, ramadan_extreme),
               names_to = "type",
               values_to = "count")

ggplot(yearly_summary, aes(x = as.factor(year), y = count, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.35), width = 0.35) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = count,
      y = count
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.70),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("total_extreme"   = "#999999", 
               "ramadan_extreme" = "#d73027"),
    labels = c("total_extreme"   = "Full Year", 
               "ramadan_extreme" = "Ramadan")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Extreme Temperature Days",
    title = "Extreme Temperature Days in Ramadan vs. Full Year",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
